lines.say: This NES game sold 4 million copies, and one level made almost everyone quit.
Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles came out in 1989, right as the cartoon was exploding.
Konami made it, but in America it shipped under their second label, Ultra Games.
You control all four turtles, and you can switch between them any time by pressing start.
Each one has a different weapon: swords, nunchucks, a bo staff, and sai.
You explore the city from above, then drop into side-scrolling buildings and sewers.
Then comes level two. You swim through a dam to disarm eight time bombs.
You get just two minutes and twenty seconds, and the walls are lined with electric seaweed.
For a lot of kids, that's where the game ended.
It still sold more than 4 million copies worldwide.
In Europe, the word ninja was a problem, so it became Teenage Mutant Hero Turtles.
In Japan, its title translates roughly to: Legend of the Radical Ninja Turtles.

args.text: LEGEND OF THE RADICAL NINJA TURTLES

lines.say: And the computer version had a jump that was impossible to make without cheating.
Later that year, Konami's arcade Turtles game gave fans the four-player brawler they really wanted.
Did you ever beat the dam? Follow for more 8-Bit Backstory!
